_preregistration.follows: F129: lambda_ca has a real but unrankable spread and is blind to RWKV

verdict: RUNG (F64 reproduced, not assumed): at r2.T0.02 RWKV's attractor share is 0.1647 against a median of 0.9336 across the PILE-TRAINED attention models (corpus controlled, as F64's claim requires), a gap of +0.7689 (required >= 0.1). F64's architectural effect is recovered, so this measurement is reading the attractor and the comparison below is licensed. PRIMARY (signal): top1 6/6, distinct 6/6, rep2 6/6. top1 spread/noise: r2.T0.02=38.86, r2.T0.2=43.54, r2.T0.7=9.57, r3.T0.02=13.58, r3.T0.2=8.14, r3.T0.7=13.61. SEED-STABLE RANKING: top1=0.8483, distinct=0.7907, rep2=0.7503 (threshold 0.6). SECONDARY (invariance, asked only where signal AND a stable ranking both hold): top1=+0.752, distinct=+0.737, rep2=+0.654. MODEL-ATTRIBUTABLE: ['top1', 'distinct', 'rep2']. The attractor share ranks models the same way across constructions where lambda_ca could not, so the failure in F129 is specific to lambda_ca rather than general to the instrument -- and the results built on the share (F63/F64, F86, F117/F120/F121) rest on the quantity that survives. CONTRAST with lambda_ca (F129): signal 2/4 constructions, seed-stable ranking 0.0303, and blind to RWKV (mid-pack at +0.135 despite having no attractor). Neither readout's number means much alone; the comparison is the point. BOUNDARY: 10 models differing in SIZE as well as family, 6 constructions, N=48, settle=30. A share that survives here is model-attributable across THESE constructions, not in general.
